t.1.134.1: Then all the citizens from the city of Vāraṇāvata, furnished with every auspicious thing, came forth tirelessly, in accordance with the scriptures.
t.1.134.2: Hearing that the sons of Pāṇḍu had arrived, the people came out by the thousands in various conveyances; the moment they heard it, they went with the greatest joy to meet those best of men.
t.1.134.3: Those people of Vāraṇāvata, having approached the sons of Kuntī, all uttered blessings for their victory, and surrounding them, waited upon them.
t.1.134.4: Surrounded by them, Yudhiṣṭhira, the tiger among men, the King of Dharma, shone forth like a god, like Vajrapāṇi surrounded by the immortals.
t.1.134.5: Honored by the townspeople, and having honored the townspeople in turn, the sinless ones entered Vāraṇāvata, which was adorned and thronged with people.
t.1.134.6: Having entered the city, those heroes then went swiftly to the houses of brāhmaṇas devoted to their own duties, O lord of the earth.
t.1.134.7: Those best of men also visited the houses of the city's officials and of the chariot-warriors, and even the houses of the vaiśyas and śūdras.
t.1.134.8: And the Pāṇḍavas, bulls among the Bharatas, having been honored by the men of the city, afterwards went to their dwelling, with Purocana leading the way.
t.1.134.9: That Purocana gave them foods, rice and drinks, fine beds, and excellent seats.
t.1.134.10: There, honored by him and provided with very costly furnishings, they lived, attended upon by the men who dwelt in the town.
t.1.134.11: When they had dwelt there for ten nights, Purocana then announced to them the house called "Auspicious," which was inauspicious.
t.1.134.12: There, at Purocana's word, those tigers among men entered with all their belongings, as the Guhyakas enter Kailāsa.
t.1.134.14: Clearly, scorcher of foes, this house has been made to be set on fire, for hemp and resin have plainly been brought in for its construction. All the material, the muñja grass, balvaja grass, bamboo and the rest, has been soaked in ghee.
t.1.134.13: But Yudhiṣṭhira, skilled in all dharma, having looked closely at that house, said thus to Bhīmasena, "It is made to burn, gentle one!" as he smelled the odor of fat and ghee mixed with lac.
t.1.134.15: For it has been well built by trusted craftsmen, skilled in the work of house-building; this wicked Purocana wishes to burn me while I trust him.
t.1.134.16: But the greatly wise Vidura foresaw this very calamity at that time; therefore, O Pārtha, he warned me beforehand.
t.1.134.17: Warned by him, we have come to know that this inauspicious house was skillfully built by secret craftsmen who are subject to Duryodhana's will.
t.1.134.18: Since you, sir, believe that this house has been built to be set on fire, it would be well for us to go back to the very place where we lived before.
t.1.134.20: For if Purocana should detect our true intent, he would then act swiftly and burn us even by force.
t.1.134.19: I think it best that we dwell here, watchful and betraying no sign of our purpose, as though we had already perished, while we search for a sure and desired way of escape from this place.
t.1.134.21: This Purocana fears neither public reproach nor unrighteousness; for so the fool behaves, standing under the control of Suyodhana.
t.1.134.23: But if we, fearing the fire, were to flee, Suyodhana, greedy for the kingdom, would have us all killed by his spies.
t.1.134.22: And if we were burned here, would grandfather Bhīṣma become angry, or for what reason would he provoke the Kauravas to anger? He might be angered, thinking “this is a matter of dharma,” and so too might the other bulls among the Kurus.
t.1.134.25: Therefore, deceiving this wicked one and that wicked Suyodhana, we must live here and there in a hidden dwelling.
t.1.134.26: Let us, then, roam this earth as men devoted to the hunt; in that way the paths will become known to us when we flee.
t.1.134.24: Standing firm in his position while they have none, backed by allies while they have none, and possessed of a great treasury as against one whose treasury is depleted, he would surely have them killed by his stratagems.
t.1.134.28: We must act unwearyingly, so that neither Purocana nor any of the townspeople may come to know that we are dwelling here.
t.1.134.27: Let us this very day make a well-concealed hole in the ground; there, as we breathe in hiding, the fire will not burn us up.
